entries.text: Hereditary monarchies are easier to hold than new ones.
A ruler should not change the established order unless absolutely necessary.
A ruler should not expect to keep the friendship of the people he has occupied.
A ruler should not try to give the people more than they expected.
A ruler should not try to be tough with the people he needs to maintain power.
A ruler should not occupy a new territory without considering the local customs and institutions.
A ruler should not underestimate the difficulty of holding onto a new possession in a foreign land.
A ruler should prioritize establishing colonies in the new territory to ensure loyalty and stability.
A ruler should not plunder the new territory, but rather live among its people to improve security and stability.
A ruler must eliminate the family of the previous ruler to secure power.
A ruler must leave existing laws in place to avoid provoking the population.
A ruler must not restrict themselves to dealing with present threats but must use every means to foresee and forestall future problems.
A ruler must not allow foreign powers to gain influence in the new territory.
A ruler must either pamper people or destroy them; harming them just a little will lead to retaliation.
A ruler must not provoke more hostility by moving an army and requisitioning lodgings, as it can turn the entire population into enemies.
A ruler must not put off war when they see trouble coming, as it can lead to the enemy gaining the upper hand.
A ruler must not make mistakes in other departments, as it can undermine their position and lead to loss of allies and territory.
To help another ruler grow powerful is to prepare your own ruin.
A ruler should not put their faith in their own foresight and spirit, as time can quickly turn against them.
A ruler should not underestimate the power of their enemies, as they can quickly shift in favor of their opponents.
To conquer a country like Turkey, it is hard to conquer but once conquered, it is very easy to hold.
To conquer a country like France, it is somewhat easy to conquer but very hard to hold.
A country with no barons to invite you in and no one to make your invasion easier by rebelling against the king is hard to conquer.
When invading a state, consider its type and internal divisions.
If a state is accustomed to self-government, destroy it to hold it.
Unity among the invading forces is crucial for success.
The new ruler's own forces should be used to conquer the state.
The old local rulers' families should be eliminated to establish authority.
A ruler must be able to choose a new leader from among themselves to maintain stability.
A ruler must be able to live in freedom without one to maintain stability.
A ruler must be able to impose a new administrative system and procedures to establish their government and guarantee its security.
A ruler must be able to rely on their own resources to achieve their goals.

{'name': 'Be Self-Reliant', 'description': 'A leader should be self-reliant and not rely on others for support.'}
{'name': 'Adapt to Changing Circumstances', 'description': 'A leader must be able to adapt to changing circumstances to succeed.'}
{'name': 'The rule of the lucky', 'description': 'A ruler who achieves power through luck rather than their own abilities is unlikely to be able to hold on to it.'}
{'name': 'The importance of a strong foundation', 'description': 'A ruler who fails to establish a strong foundation for their power is unlikely to be able to maintain it.'}
A ruler should not rely solely on their own abilities, but also seek the counsel of others.
A ruler should be aware of the potential for rebellion and take steps to prevent it.
A ruler should be willing to use force to maintain control, but also be aware of the potential consequences of such actions.
A ruler should be aware of the importance of building alliances and securing the support of key individuals.
A ruler should be willing to make difficult decisions and take calculated risks to achieve their goals.
Eliminate potential threats to power
Win the support of key allies
Secure territory before the death of a powerful figure
Block unwanted papal initiatives
Overcome obstacles by force or fraud
A ruler should aim to be the master of all Tuscany.
A ruler should not allow a cardinal whose interests they have damaged to win the election.
A ruler should not allow a cardinal who would have reason to fear them to win the election.
A ruler should choose a Spanish pope if possible.
A ruler should not let a powerful cardinal like the cardinal of Rouen take the throne.
To achieve power, one must be willing to take risks and make tough decisions.
Working with others can be demeaning and may not be necessary for achieving power.
Killing fellow citizens and betraying friends can be effective means of achieving power, but may not bring glory.
A strong personality and ability to take charge are essential for achieving power.
Power can be maintained through violence and manipulation, but may not be sustainable in the long term.
When taking hold of a state, a ruler must assess how much violence and cruelty will be necessary.
A ruler should get the necessary violence and cruelty over with at once, to avoid being cruel on a regular basis.
A ruler should use the power given to them to deliver maximum benefits to their subjects.
A ruler must have the support of either the common people or the nobles to maintain power.
A king who comes to power with the support of the people can get by without the nobles, but a king who gets there with the support of the nobles will have trouble keeping it.
A ruler who takes the people under his protection will find it easy to win their loyalty.
A ruler who becomes king against the will of the majority and with the support of the wealthy nobles must make it a priority to win over the affection of the common people.
{'name': 'Defend with own resources', 'description': 'A ruler should be able to defend themselves with their own resources.'}
{'name': 'Fortify home towns', 'description': 'A ruler should encourage their citizens to fortify their home towns.'}
{'name': 'Maintain public supplies', 'description': 'A ruler should maintain public supplies to keep their citizens well-fed.'}
A ruler who can't take on an enemy in the field but has to withdraw behind their city walls will always be in need of outside help.
A ruler who has built good fortifications and managed their relationship with their subjects will always think twice before attacking them.
A well-fortified town with a ruler who doesn't inspire hatred among their subjects won't be attacked, and even if they are, their attackers will leave humiliated.
Papal succession can lead to a loss of power and influence.
The Church's power can be increased by the use of finance and force.
The use of mercenaries can lead to a prolonged dependence on foreign armies.
Mercenaries are useless and dangerous for defense.
A ruler or republic must not rely on mercenaries for defense.
A ruler or republic must have good laws and good armed forces to ensure stability and security.
A ruler or republic must go in person and act as commander themselves to ensure effective defense.
A republic must send its citizens to fight, and if a commander is not good, they must replace him.
{'name': 'Hire Local Forces', 'description': 'Hiring local forces is more effective and reliable than hiring mercenaries.'}
{'name': 'Avoid Auxiliary Armies', 'description': 'Auxiliary armies are ineffective and may be counterproductive.'}
{'name': 'Mercenaries are a No-Win Situation', 'description': 'Using mercenaries guarantees ruin, as they are a tightly knit force and every one of them obedient to someone else.'}

{'name': 'Auxiliaries are More Dangerous than Mercenaries', 'description': 'Auxiliaries are far more dangerous than mercenaries, as they are a tightly knit force and every one of them obedient to someone else.'}
{'name': 'Rely on Your Own Troops', 'description': 'Rulers should prefer to lose with their own troops than to win with others, as a victory won with foreign forces is not a real victory at all.'}
{'name': 'No Mercenaries Rule', 'description': 'A state should not rely on mercenaries or auxiliaries, as they are unreliable and can lead to ruin.'}
{'name': 'Own Resources Rule', 'description': 'A ruler should rely on their own resources and men, rather than foreign forces, to maintain power and stability.'}
{'name': 'Composite Forces Rule', 'description': 'A state with a mix of its own men and mercenaries is better than one relying solely on mercenaries or auxiliaries.'}
{'name': 'Rule 1: A State Must Have Its Own Army', 'description': 'A state without its own army is not secure and its ruler is not a true leader.'}
{'name': 'Rule 2: A Ruler Must Involve Himself in Military Matters', 'description': 'A ruler who does not involve himself in military matters will not have the respect and trust of his soldiers.'}

{'name': 'Rule 3: A Ruler Must Exercise His Mind', 'description': 'A ruler must exercise his mind by reading history, studying the strategies and achievements of great leaders, and learning from their successes and failures.'}
